title: Does `research-finding` own anything irreducible, or is it a projection?
statement: Is there state a research-finding artifact would hold that is not already held by evidence(kind: source), assertion, or question — and that something downstream must traverse (#41)?
notes: SECOND PARTIAL RESULT, 2026-08-18 — a READING-based stage 3 was run (QST-0004, the Next.js debt), which is the case the first result said was missing. It still needed no research-finding. Source inventory: three evidence(kind: source) records, each carrying its citations in evidence.sources. Claims: three assertions, each scoped by targetEnvironment to the mode it is about. ⚠️ CONTRADICTORY SOURCES WERE ENCOUNTERED — the case this type's strongest argument rests on. Two pages of the SAME official documentation give the same operation opposite treatment: the previous-model guide says pages in development are never cached, while the Cache Components page says a synchronous fs read is a predictable value prerendered into the static shell. ⚠️ AND THE CONTRADICTION DISSOLVED RATHER THAN NEEDING A HOME. The two sources do not disagree; they describe two different modes. Scoping each assertion's targetEnvironment by cacheComponents enabled/disabled resolved it completely — which is what targetEnvironment is for, and it is the same move that fixed AST-0003. So 'contradictory sources resolved or surfaced' was satisfied by SCOPING THE CLAIMS, not by a narrative artifact. Still not conclusive: this contradiction was RESOLVABLE. A genuine unresolved disagreement between authorities — two sources making incompatible claims about the SAME configuration — has not yet been met, and that remains the one case research-finding might own. Remains unanswered, with the evidence against it now covering both the experimental and the documentary half of stage 3.
